papers.title_in_file: Photon Conversion and Interaction on Chip
papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper reporting 65% external quantum efficiency sum-frequency generation and a single-photon-level coupling measurement in a periodically poled thin-film lithium niobate microring.

assertions.value: The authors report an external quantum efficiency of (65 ± 3)% at an on-chip pump power of (104 ± 4) µW in their periodically poled lithium niobate microring.
quotes: (65 ± 3)% quantum efﬁciency is achieved with at (104 ± 4) µW pump power
assertions.reader_inference: The quoted sentence is grammatically garbled in the source ("achieved with at"); the figures are consistent with the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that, taking into account all insertion losses on and off chip, the peak conversion corresponds to about 9% total efficiency.
quotes: this corresponds to about 9% total
assertions.reader_inference: The 65% figure is an on-chip external quantum efficiency; the 9% figure is the system-level number including fiber and detector-side losses.

assertions.value: The authors report an on-chip noise photon flux of 0.3 MHz under continuous-wave pumping at the 65% peak quantum efficiency, and a noise of 3 × 10−5 photons per pulse for pulses of about 100 ps that match the cavity lifetime.
quotes: If using ∼100 ps pulses that match the cavity lifetime
At the 65% peak QE, the onchip noise photon ﬂux is 0.3 MHz under continuous-wave pumping.
the noise photon per pulse is 3 × 10−5
assertions.reader_inference: The measurement was made with continuous-wave pumping; the per-pulse figure follows from 0.3 MHz times 100 ps, which is 3 × 10-5, and was not measured with pulses.

assertions.value: The authors report that the noise photon flux increases between quadratically and cubically with pump power, and the figure caption fits it as Nnoise proportional to P to the power 2.4.
assertions.anchor: Low-noise Frequency Conversion, p.5; Fig. 3 caption
quotes: the increase of the noise photon ﬂux is between quadratic and cubic with the pump power
Solid black line is ﬁtted to the pump power P as Nnoise ∼ P 2.4.

assertions.value: The authors state that the noise scaling indicates that, besides Raman scattering, a cascaded spontaneous parametric down-conversion and sum-frequency generation process is also present.
quotes: This result indicates that besides Raman scattering, the cascaded SPDC and SFG process also presents
assertions.reader_inference: The attribution rests on the fitted exponent alone; no separate measurement of each noise channel is reported.

assertions.value: The authors state that the noise level at peak conversion meets the requirement of quantum applications using single-photon pulses.
quotes: which meets the requirement of quantum applications using single-photon pulses

assertions.value: The authors state that the noise level can be substantially lowered by, for example, further detuning the pump from the signal, citing a prior work; this was not tested in the paper.
quotes: This noise level can be substantially lowered by, for example, further detuning the pump from the signal [24].

assertions.value: The authors report an on-chip quantum efficiency of about 10−5 at one mean intracavity pump photon, with the intracavity signal photon number fixed at 0.25 (photon fluxes Np = 2.8 GHz and Ns = 0.7 GHz), after correcting for coupling loss and detector efficiency.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5; Fig. 4
quotes: The on-chip quantum eﬃciency is about 10−5 when there is one pump photon on average in the cavity
is achieved at one intracavity pump photon (corresponding to photon ﬂux Np = 2.8 GHz)
where the intracavity signal photon number is ﬁxed at 0.25 (corresponding to photon ﬂux Ns = 0.7 GHz)
assertions.reader_inference: Pump and signal are weak coherent states, so 'one photon' is a mean intracavity number, not a Fock-state result.

assertions.value: The authors report a linear dependence of the quantum efficiency on the intracavity pump photon number in the single-photon regime.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5; Fig. 4
quotes: we observe linear dependency of the quantum eﬃciency on the intracavity pump photon number

assertions.value: The authors extract a photon-photon coupling coefficient g of 9.1 MHz from the single-photon-level measurement by fitting the coupled-mode equations, compared with 8.2 MHz from the classical measurement.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5; Fig. 4
quotes: g to be 9.1 MHz, compared to 8.2 MHz as from the classical measurement
assertions.reader_inference: The coupled-mode fit has g as its only free parameter, so g depends on the other fixed device parameters in Table S1.

assertions.value: The authors report that fitting the steady-state solution of the coupled-mode equations to the classical data gives a photon-photon coupling coefficient g of 8.2 MHz.
quotes: g is determined to be 8.2 MHz

assertions.value: The authors state that the slightly higher g from the single-photon-level data may come from better quasi-phase matching or triple resonance for single-photon light waves, due to the absence of thermo-optical and photorefractive effects.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: This slightly higher value may come from better QPM or triple resonance for single-photon light waves
assertions.reader_inference: Offered as a possible cause; the paper reports no test of it.

assertions.value: The authors report an internal Rabi rotation angle of 0.01 per pump photon, from g = 9.1 × 106 (exponent printed flat; 9.1 MHz) and Qp,i = 7.1 × 105 (exponent printed flat).
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: In our case, g = 9.1 × 106 and Qp,i = 7.1 × 105, so that θ = 0.01

assertions.value: The paper defines the internal Rabi rotation angle as theta = 2 g Qp,i / omega_p, the Rabi rotation a pump photon induces between signal and sum-frequency photons while it is lost in the cavity.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5; Supplement A
quotes: the internal Rabi rotation angle θ = 2gQp,i/ωp
θ then gives how much Rabi rotation can a pump photon induce during it is lost in the cavity
assertions.certainty_reason: Defined in the main text and the supplement.

assertions.value: The authors state that increasing theta to π/2 would require improving the intrinsic pump Q to 108 (exponent printed flat), which they say has been demonstrated in polished thin-film lithium niobate microdisks (cited).
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: Increasing θ to π/2 would require improving Qp,i to 108, which has been demonstrated in polished TFLN microdisks [18].
assertions.reader_inference: The microdisk Q is attributed to a preprint [18]; no calculation of the required improvement is shown.

assertions.value: The authors state that, based on the current nonlinear parameters, a cavity quality factor of 108 (exponent printed flat) will enable a C-NOT gate between single photons.
quotes: Based on the current nonlinear parameters, a cavity qualify factor of 108
will enable C-NOT gate between single photons
assertions.reader_inference: No gate fidelity or derivation is given.

assertions.value: The authors state that a single pump photon can produce 0.01 internal Rabi rotation angle, which they describe as already appreciable from a fundamental standpoint.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5; Discussion, p.6
quotes: a single photon can produce 0.01 internal Rabi rotation angle
which is already appreciable from a fundamental standpoint

assertions.value: The authors state that the microring has a radius of 80 µm and a cross-section of 600 nm in height and 1700 nm in top-width.
quotes: we use a microring with a radius of 80 µm and a cross-section of 600 nm in height and 1700 nm in top-width
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device geometry.

assertions.value: The authors state that the pump and signal are in the telecom C-band and the sum-frequency light is in the visible band; they select modes at 1560.15 nm (pump), 1551.85 nm and 778.00 nm, with azimuthal orders mp = 602, ms = 606, mf = 1357 and poling number M = 149.
assertions.anchor: Device design and Device characterization, pp.3-4
quotes: The pump and signal are both in the telecom C-band and their SF is in the visible band
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own mode selection.

assertions.value: The authors state that all three waves are in the fundamental quasi-transverse-magnetic modes and interact through the largest nonlinear tensor element d33 with over 90% mode overlap.
quotes: all three waves are in the fundamental quasi-transverse-magnetic (quasi-TM) modes and interact through TFLN’s largest nonlinear tensor d33 with over 90% mode overlap
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device operation.

assertions.value: The authors state a concentric periodically poled region with period of 3.37 µm given by Λ = 2πR/M with M = 149 and near 50% duty cycle, made with several 1-ms and 450-V electrical pulses.
quotes: a concentric periodically-poled region with period of Λ = 3.37 µm given by Λ = 2πR/M , M = 149 and near 50% duty cycle
via several 1-ms and 450-V electrical pulses
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own fabrication.

assertions.value: The authors state that the device is made on a magnesium-doped Z-cut lithium niobate on insulator wafer with a 600-nm thick film on 2 µm silicon dioxide, and shallow etch of 430 nm leaving 170 nm with a sidewall angle of approximately 64◦.
quotes: magnesium-doped Z-cut LNOI wafer (NANOLN Inc.), with a 600-nm thick LN thin ﬁlm bonded on 2 µm silicon dioxide layer
430-nm thick LN is etched with 170-nm LN remaining
angle is approximately 64◦
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own fabrication.

assertions.value: The authors state the pulley coupler has top width 400 nm, gap 650 nm and length 40 µm, to give overcoupling for both visible and infrared light.
quotes: the pulley top width of wpulley = 400 nm, the gap of gpulley = 650 nm, and the length of Lpulley = 40 µm
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own coupler design.

assertions.value: The authors state that the pulley top width is fixed by requiring npRp = nrRr; for the sum-frequency wave the coupling strength is proportional to the pulley length and inversely proportional to the gap, and for the signal mode it varies as sinc of the coupling phase mismatch.
quotes: requiring npRp = nrRr [22]
the waveguidemicroring coupling strength is proportional to the length of the pulley coupler, while inversely proportional to their gap
the coupling strength varies as sinc(∆Φ)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own design method.

assertions.value: The authors report fiber-chip-fiber coupling losses of 8 ± 0.15 dB at 1556 nm and 9.5 ± 0.2 dB at 778 nm.
quotes: The ﬁber-chip-ﬁber coupling losses are measured to be 8 ± 0.15 dB at 1556 nm and 9.5 ± 0.2 dB at 778 nm

assertions.value: The paper defines the external quantum efficiency as Nf over Ns, with Ns the number of input signal photons to the cavity and Nf the number of converted sum-frequency photons at the cavity output.
quotes: where Ns is the number of input signal photons to the cavity and Nf is that of converted SF photons at the cavity output

assertions.value: The paper gives the effective Hamiltonian for sum-frequency generation between single modes, and states that g is the photon-photon coupling strength, interpreted as the effective Rabi frequency produced by a pump photon.
quotes: g is the photon-photon coupling strength, which can be interpreted as the effective Rabi frequency produced by a pump photon

assertions.value: The authors state that the delta function in the photon-photon coupling expression accounts for quasi-phase matching by periodic poling, where mj are azimuthal orders of the cavity modes and M is the azimuthal poling grating number.
quotes: accounts for quasi-phase matching (QPM) by periodic poling

assertions.value: The authors state, citing prior work, that under quasi-phase matching and triple resonance the maximum quantum efficiency is given by an expression in the loaded and coupling quality factors of the signal and sum-frequency modes.
quotes: Under QPM and triple resonance (see Supplementary Material A), the maximum QE is given by [21]:
where Qj,o is the quality factor with o = c, l denoting the coupling and loaded Q, respectively.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer garbles Eq. (4); the form appears to be the product of Qs,l/Qs,c and Qf,l/Qf,c.

assertions.value: The authors report that with a maximum quantum efficiency of about 65% and a normalized transduction efficiency of about 4.5%/µW the optimal pump power is around 115 µW.
quotes: In our case, ηQmEax ≈ 65% and ηtnroarn ≈ 4.5%/µW, so that the optimal power is around 115 µW.
assertions.reader_inference: The measured peak was at (104 ± 4) µW, near the 115 µW prediction.

assertions.value: The authors report a normalized power transduction efficiency fitted to about 4.5% per µW in the low conversion region.
quotes: the normalized power transduction eﬃciency is ﬁtted to be about 4.5% µW−1

assertions.value: The authors state that the measured quality factors give a highest possible external quantum efficiency of about 65%, and that an even higher efficiency requires the cavity to be further overcoupled.
quotes: give the highest possibl external quantum eﬃciency of ηQmEax ≈ 65%
For an even higher eﬃciency, the cavity needs to be further overcoupled.

assertions.value: The authors state that previous demonstrations used critical coupling, and that for practical applications the cavity should be overcoupled so photons are extracted before significant cavity loss.
quotes: This is in contrast to previous demonstrations, where critical coupling was adopted
one instead needs to over-couple the cavity so that the photons can be extracted out before signiﬁcantly lost in the cavity

assertions.value: The authors state that under critical coupling most of the input power and about half of the converted photons are lost inside the cavity, giving a low quantum efficiency and prohibiting cascaded operations.
quotes: most of the input power and about half of the converted photons are lost inside the cavity

assertions.value: The authors state that the 1560.15 nm mode is designated as the pump to reduce the Raman background.
quotes: To reduce the Raman background, we designate the 1560.15 nm mode to the pump.

assertions.value: The authors report a clean spectrum with low baseline, except a residual second-harmonic peak at about 780 nm that is significant only in the high conversion regime (above 50%) and is rejected by a bandpass filter of about 3 nm centered at 778 nm.
quotes: It exhibits a clean proﬁle with low baseline, except for a residual second-harmonic peak at ∼780 nm by the strong pump.
This peak is signiﬁcant only in the high conversion regime (i.e.,>50%)
we reject it using a ∼3 nm bandpass ﬁlter centered at 778 nm

assertions.value: The caption of the spectrum figure reports on-chip powers of pump, signal and sum-frequency waves of -13.8 dBm, -44.3 dBm and -44.0 dBm after correcting for coupling loss.
quotes: the on-chip power of pump, signal and SF waves are -13.8 dBm, -44.3 dBm and -44.0 dBm, respectively
assertions.reader_inference: -13.8 dBm is about 42 µW, not the 104 µW of the peak; the spectrum is at a different operating point from the peak.

assertions.value: The authors report a fixed on-chip signal power of about 37 nW with the pump increased gradually, and that temperature within 45 ± 0.3 ◦C and laser wavelengths within ± 20 pm were slightly tuned to compensate for phase mismatch and resonance drift.
quotes: the signal power is ﬁxed to be about 37 nW on chip
we only need to slightly optimize the temperature within 45 ± 0.3 ◦C and tune the wavelengths of both lasers within ± 20 pm

assertions.value: The authors state that fine temperature tuning of about 0.01 ◦C is applied to compensate for resonant mismatch due to fabrication error.
quotes: temperature tuning (∼ 0.01 ◦C) is applied to compensate for any resonant mismatch

assertions.value: The authors state that noise was measured with only the pump applied, through free-space filters, onto a silicon single-photon detector with 50% efficiency and 250 Hz dark count.
assertions.anchor: Low-noise Frequency Conversion, p.4; Supplement B
quotes: we measure the noise
(Si-SPD, quantum eﬃciency: 50%, dark count: 250 Hz)

assertions.value: The authors state a total detection efficiency for sum-frequency photons of about 17%, from a detector efficiency of about 50% and a coupling efficiency of about 33.5%, with the free-space filters removed and a lensed fiber used.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: η = ηdηc ≈ 17%, with detector eﬃciency ηd ∼ 50% and coupling eﬃciency ηc ∼ 33.5%

assertions.value: The authors report that with the signal blocked, photon counts stay at the dark count level of about 250 Hz even at the highest on-chip flux of about 5 GHz.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: we block the signal and verify that even at the highest on-chip ﬂux (∼ 5 GHz), the photon counts remain at its dark count level (∼ 250 Hz)

assertions.value: The Fig. 4 caption states that detector dark counts of 250 Hz were subtracted and coupling loss of 4.75 dB and detector efficiency of 50% accounted for.
quotes: Detector dark counts of 250 Hz have been subtracted, and the coupling loss of 4.75 dB and detector eﬃciency of 50% have been accounted for.

assertions.value: The authors state that input photon fluxes were monitored with superconducting nanowire detectors (85% efficiency, 100 Hz dark count) with about 50 dB attenuation per monitor channel because of a saturation rate of about 20 MHz.
quotes: Due to limited photon-count saturation rate (∼20 MHz)
(ID Quantique, ID281, eﬃciency 85%, dark count 100 Hz)
each monitor channel has about 50 dB attenuation

assertions.value: The authors state that error bars on efficiency and pump power come from coupling instability, and that all other error bars assume Poissonian photon counting statistics.
quotes: The error bars in left-axis and x-axis are estimated according to coupling instability.
All error bars are estimated assuming Poissonian photon counting statistics.

assertions.value: The authors state that the coupled-mode equations neglect Rayleigh backscattering and assume the single-mode condition, and are solved numerically with a time split-step method.
quotes: neglecting Rayleigh backscattering and assuming the single-mode condition
We implement time split-step method to numerically solve the coupled-mode equations.

assertions.value: Table S1 lists, in MHz (×2π), total/intrinsic/coupling dissipation rates of 1467.9/270.8/1197.0 for the pump mode, 1510.3/304.4/1205.9 for the signal mode and 1512.2/318.7/1193.5 for the sum-frequency mode.
Table S1 lists a mode area of 1.0 µm2 (exponent printed flat), and an effective nonlinear susceptibility of 18.2 pm/V among its values; the fitted g values are 8.2 MHz and 9.1 MHz.
quotes: The ﬁtted ga and gb are 8.2 MHz and 9.1 MHz, respectively.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer does not show which susceptibility (16.4 or 18.2 pm/V) goes with which figure beyond the table note a and b.

assertions.value: Table I lists this work as a periodically poled lithium niobate microring for sum-frequency generation with loaded Q values of 1.3/1.3/2.6 (units as in the table header), conversion efficiency 65% and pump power 0.1 mW.
quotes: The state-of-the-art frequency conversion in χ(2) and χ(3) cavities.

assertions.value: Table I lists a prior aluminum nitride microring sum-frequency generation result (the third listed reference by row order) with loaded Q values 3.0/3.0/1.4, conversion efficiency 42% and pump power 35 mW.
assertions.reader_inference: The row-to-reference mapping is by the order of the Ref. line.

assertions.value: Table I lists a prior silicon nitride microring four-wave-mixing Bragg scattering result (the first listed reference by row order) with conversion efficiency 60% and pump powers 50 & 8 mW.
Table I lists prior periodically poled lithium niobate microring second-harmonic results with conversion efficiencies of 10% at 0.3 mW and 26% at 1.8 mW.
The Table I caption states that it only includes works whose conversion efficiency is over 10%.
quotes: This table only includes those whose conversion eﬃciency is over 10%.

assertions.value: The authors claim orders of magnitude improvement over the state of the art across all existing photonic platforms (Table I) and, in the abstract, an improvement by over one order of magnitude.
quotes: marking orders of magnitude improvement over the state of the art across all existing photonic platforms
improving the state-of-the-art by over one order of magnitude
assertions.reader_inference: Table I shows prior conversion efficiencies up to 60%, so the improvement is mainly in pump power, not in efficiency.

assertions.value: The authors state they excluded a recent preprint's reported second-harmonic efficiency of 33% from Table I because, from its reported normalized efficiency of 602%/mW, the required pump power exceeds the claimed value.
quotes: SHG of ηcon = 33% [18]. According to its reported normalized eﬃciency of 602%/mW, the required pump power shall be
table due to this apparent inconsistence.
assertions.reader_inference: This is the authors' criticism of another work; the paper does not verify it against that work.

assertions.value: The authors state that prior thin-film lithium niobate microresonator performance was capped by relatively small χ(2) susceptibilities (e.g., d31 about 4.7 pm/V), poor mode overlapping, and low photon-extraction efficiency, and that there had been no direct demonstration of photon conversion and interaction.
quotes: relatively small χ(2) susceptibilities (e.g., d31 ∼ 4.7 pm/V) [15], poor mode overlapping [16, 18]
there has been no direct demonstration.

assertions.value: The authors state their device interacts through the largest susceptibility element, d33 of about 27 pm/V, in fundamental modes with nearly perfect overlap.
quotes: interact through TFLN’s largest χ(2) susceptibility tensor element (e.g., d33 ∼ 27 pm/V)

assertions.value: The authors claim the measured single-photon-level quantum efficiency of about 10−5 beats the best previously reported efficiency of 10−7 (cited) and breaks the record by 100 times.
quotes: the external quantum eﬃciency for signal photon conversion is ∼ 10−5
while the best eﬃciency reported hitherto is 10−7 [20]
breaking the record by 100 times
assertions.reader_inference: The prior value is cited from another group's work with broadband coherent states; setups differ.

assertions.value: The authors state that the weak photon-photon interaction prohibits the construction of nonlinear photon-photon gates, forming a bottleneck for scalable quantum computers at room temperature.
quotes: It also prohibits the construction of nonlinear photon-photon gates, thus forming a bottleneck for the development of scalable quantum computers at room temperature [6].

assertions.value: The authors state that, compared with third-order nonlinear materials, thin-film lithium niobate possesses exceptionally large second-order nonlinearity producing orders of magnitude stronger effects.
quotes: TFLN is centro-asymmetric and possesses exceptionally large second-order nonlinearity

assertions.value: The authors present a design (Fig. 5) for a thin-film lithium niobate chip for heralded entanglement generation following a cited scheme, combining a poled waveguide for photon pairs, filter microrings, directional couplers and a poled microring for sum-frequency conversion.
quotes: in Fig. 5 we present the design of an integrated chip for heralded entanglement generation, following the scheme in [2]
assertions.reader_inference: Fig. 5 is an illustration; no integrated-chip data is reported.

assertions.value: The authors state that with 12 pm net filtering bandwidth and 100 ps pump pulses the pair production is 1% per pulse per channel, and the heralding rate can approach 10 Hz at the demonstrated 10−5 conversion, orders of magnitude above previous demonstrations.
quotes: In this design, with 12 pm net ﬁltering bandwidth and 100 ps pump pulses
the SPDC at 1% photon pair production rate per pulse for each channel
The heralding rate can approach 10 Hz for the demonstrated 10−5 photon conversion

assertions.value: The authors state the scheme is deterministic in that, upon heralding, the entangled photon pair exists with near certainty, unlike spontaneous-parametric-down-conversion schemes with linear optical Bell state measurement capped at 50% success.
quotes: where the success probability is fundamentally capped at 50% [35]
this scheme is deterministic in that upon heralding, the entangled photon pair exists with nearly certainty

assertions.value: The authors state that there is still a good journey before the finish line and that strong photon-photon interaction requires further improving the cavity quality.
quotes: While there is still a good journey to take before hitting the
ther improving the cavity quality, strong photon-photon interaction is within sight
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated by the authors in the Introduction.
assertions.reader_inference: The second quote starts mid-word because the source breaks a word across lines.

assertions.value: The authors conclude they demonstrated photon conversion and interaction with record high efficiency and low noise, with noise attributed to deep single-mode condition and suppression of side processes, and call lithium niobate a superior platform for scalable quantum applications.
quotes: thanks to the deep single-mode condition and suppression of side processes
a superior platform of photonic integrated circuits is within sight for scalable quantum applications

assertions.value: The authors state that the pulley coupler is made to attain simultaneously overcoupling for both visible and infrared lightwaves.
quotes: to attain simultaneously overcoupling condition for both the visible and IR lightwaves
